proof.criterion: Review round 1, item 2: /healthz names the role claim view when it can answer no read, through the same state RolesHeldBy reads, without making a liveness probe a restart loop.
proof.surface: The listener's own /healthz handler over a role claim view whose watcher completes no scan (the package's timeOutRoleClaimScan, kvwatchtest.TimingOut on every watch).
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... go test ./cmd/listener/ -count=1 -run '^TestHealthzReportsARoleClaimViewThatCompletesNoScanDegraded$' -timeout 10m, then the same with -overlay pointing cmd/listener/main.go at its content at d94de21c (the commit before this change), then the whole healthz and self-health family: go test ./cmd/listener/ -count=1 -run 'Healthz|SelfHealth' -v.
proof.observed: ok at the head. Against the previous main.go: '--- FAIL ... /healthz over a role claim view that completed no scan = 200 map[... status:healthy], want 200 degraded'. The family is 24 of 24 PASS (ok 26.099s), TestHealthzAnswersUnhealthyWhileTheInterestWatcherIsDead and the durable, JetStream-stall, live-lane and self-health monitor tests among them, so the new report displaces none of the unhealthy answers. Ping is untouched in the diff; the report reads store.Registry.RoleViewErr, which goes through the same roleViewGeneration RolesHeldBy goes through.
proof.negativeControl: Two. The overlay run against the previous main.go, which answers healthy in the state the new test puts the view in. And this phase's own probe (removed before this handoff) for the ordering the new check could have broken: with the role claim bucket's stream deleted, so the role watcher holds a terminal error, /healthz answers '503 map[error:interest KV watcher unavailable: role claims watcher stopped status:unhealthy]' while RoleViewErr reads 'the role claim view is not complete: role claims watcher stopped' - the watcher-error check still answers first, and the degraded report takes no unhealthy answer's place.

observations.what: One of the six wakeComplete call sites is bound by no test, and removing it changes nothing observable.
observations.evidence: kvwatch.go:668, the wake a replacement watch makes after it stores complete=false and clears any recorded error. With it removed, ./internal/kvwatch/... and ./internal/store/ are both green, where removing any of the other five fails a test by name. It is a wake to re-read a state that still says wait: a caller that had already read complete=true has returned nil, and one parked on an error has returned that error, so the only waiters left re-park, and the scan's own wake at 829 ends them. Harmless, and it is the one line of this work that no test holds.

observations.what: A watcher fault of the role claim bucket is reported under the interest cache's name.
observations.evidence: listenerCaches (cmd/listener/main.go) names the whole store.Registry 'interest', and Registry.WatchErr returns the interest watcher's error else the role claim watcher's, so a role claim watcher that ends answers /healthz '503 interest KV watcher unavailable: role claims watcher stopped', measured here with the role bucket's stream deleted. The status and the cause are right and only the dependency's name is wrong, and it reads the same on main: this change adds the degraded report after it and alters nothing of it.
